from.place: Proof of lem-kun-0f0f, preliminary integral tensor calculation: making comparisons between simultaneous filtered K-flat models independent of replacements; right fraction calculus used in the finite filtered resolution argument.

title: Right fraction calculus for globally finite filtered complexes
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\mathcal H_f(R)$ have as objects integer cochain complexes of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with decreasing filtrations by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration], each with some integers $a<b$ such that $F^aK=K$ and $F^bK=0$ as complexes. The bounds may depend on the object. Its morphisms are filtration-preserving chain maps modulo homotopies $h^n:K^n\to L^{n-1}$ with $f-g=dh+hd$ and $h^n(F^iK^n)\subseteq F^iL^{n-1}$. Define $\operatorname{gr}^iK=F^iK/F^{i+1}K$ [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients], and let $W$ be the morphisms inducing quasi-isomorphisms on every $\operatorname{gr}^i$.
Then $W$ contains identities, is closed under composition, satisfies two-out-of-three, and admits a calculus of right fractions. Explicitly:
(1) for $f:X\to Z$ and $s:Y\to Z$ with $s\in W$, there are $t:T\to X$ in $W$ and $g:T\to Y$ such that $f\circ t=s\circ g$ in $\mathcal H_f(R)$;
(2) for $f,g:X\to Y$ and $s:Y\to Z$ in $W$ with $s\circ f=s\circ g$, there is $t:T\to X$ in $W$ such that $f\circ t=g\circ t$.
The objects $T$ in these assertions also have a globally finite filtration; no cochain-degree bound is required.

source.place: Tags 05S1 (lemma-filtered-acyclic) and 05RM (lemma-acyclic-general), using the cone construction in Tag 05RG (lemma-construct-multiplicative-system). Restrict to globally finite filtrations, stable under shifts, finite sums and cones; cached derived.tex in /home/ubuntu/c1-stacks-review/, lines 1909 ff., 2231 ff., 4292–4317.

proof.text: First check that $W$ is well-defined on filtered homotopy classes. A filtration-preserving map or homotopy descends to every quotient $F^i/F^{i+1}$, and the identity $f-g=dh+hd$ descends as well [def-sp-filtration; def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. On a cocycle $x$ the difference is $d(hx)$, so homotopic maps have the same cohomology map. Grading and cohomology preserve identity maps and composition [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Consequently $W$ contains identities, is closed under composition, and has two-out-of-three: for each pair $(i,n)$ apply two-out-of-three for invertible module homomorphisms to $H^n(\operatorname{gr}^i f)$, $H^n(\operatorname{gr}^i g)$ and their composite. For example, if the first and composite are invertible, the second is their composite with the inverse of the first; the other case is identical with the inverse on the other side.

source.place: Tag 05S1 (lemma-filtered-acyclic), definition immediately preceding it; homotopy-invariance calculation also Homology Tag 0116 (lemma-map-cohomology-homotopy-cochain)

proof.text: Use direct-sum filtrations for all finite sums and cones, and the unchanged filtration index for shifts: $F^i(K[m])^n=(F^iK)^{n+m}$. For a filtered chain map $v:A\to B$, put $\operatorname{Cone}(v)^n=B^n\oplus A^{n+1}$ with $d(b,a)=(d_Bb+v(a),-d_Aa)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The filtration $F^iB^n\oplus F^iA^{n+1}$ is preserved by this differential. The map $[(b,a)]\mapsto([b],[a])$ identifies its associated graded complex with $\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{gr}^i v)$, since both the quotient relation and differential agree componentwise [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. The same calculation identifies grading of a finite sum or shift with the sum or shift of the graded complexes. A common lower bound is the minimum of the lower bounds of the finitely many input objects, and a common upper bound is their maximum; these bounds work for sums, shifts and cones in every cochain degree [def-sp-filtration]. Finally a shift of an acyclic complex is acyclic, since its cycles and boundaries are those of the original complex in the shifted degree (a sign in the differential changes neither).

source.place: Tag 014E (definition-cone); Tag 05S1 (lemma-filtered-acyclic), restriction to the globally finite full subcategory

proof.text: We will use the following elementary cycle calculation, rather than introduce a new lemma node. If $p:B\to A$ is a degreewise surjective chain map of $R$-module complexes whose kernel complex $E$ is acyclic, then $p$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Indeed, lift a cocycle $a\in A^n$ to $b\in B^n$; then $db$ is a cocycle in $E^{n+1}$, so $db=de$ for some $e\in E^n$ and $b-e$ is a cocycle lifting $a$. If a cocycle $b\in B^n$ maps to a boundary $da_0$, lift $a_0$ to $b_0\in B^{n-1}$; the cocycle $b-db_0$ lies in $E^n$, so it is $de_0$ for some $e_0\in E^{n-1}$ and $b=d(b_0+e_0)$. This proves surjectivity and injectivity on every cohomology module. We apply this only after passing to an individual associated graded complex, where the displayed projections below remain surjective by their direct-sum form.

source.place: Elementary module-cycle calculation for the cone constructions underlying Tag 05RG (lemma-construct-multiplicative-system), right MS2 and MS3

proof.text: For the right Ore square, choose chain representatives $f:X\to Z$ and $s:Y\to Z$. Define $T^n=X^n\oplus Y^n\oplus Z^{n-1}$ and $D(x,y,z)=(d_Xx,d_Yy,-d_Zz+f(x)-s(y))$, with componentwise filtration. The chain-map identities for $f,s$ give $D^2=0$. Let $t:T\to X$ and $g:T\to Y$ be the projections. They are filtered chain maps, and the filtered degree $-1$ map $h:T\to Z$, $h(x,y,z)=z$, satisfies $d_Zh+hD=ft-sg$; hence $ft=sg$ in $\mathcal H_f(R)$. The kernel of $t$ is the complex $(y,z)\mapsto(d_Yy,-d_Zz-s(y))$, namely $\operatorname{Cone}(s)[-1]$ after interchanging its two summands [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. In each filtration degree its associated graded is $\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{gr}^i s)[-1]$ by step 2. Because $s\in W$, the ordinary cone criterion [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic], applied to the $R$-module complexes $\operatorname{gr}^iY,\operatorname{gr}^iZ$, makes this kernel acyclic. The graded projection $\operatorname{gr}^i t$ is degreewise surjective with exactly this kernel, by the direct-sum quotient formula of step 2. Step 3 therefore makes $\operatorname{gr}^i t$ a quasi-isomorphism for every $i$, so $t\in W$.

source.place: Tags 05RG (lemma-construct-multiplicative-system), right MS2, and 014E (definition-cone); ordinary acyclic cone criterion underlying Tag 05RT (lemma-acyclic)

proof.text: For cancellation choose chain representatives and write $a=f-g:X\to Y$. The equality $sf=sg$ in the filtered homotopy category gives a filtration-preserving degree $-1$ map $H:X\to Z$ with $sa=d_ZH+Hd_X$. Set $C^n=Y^n\oplus Z^{n-1}$ and $d_C(y,z)=(d_Yy,-d_Zz-s(y))$, so $C=\operatorname{Cone}(s)[-1]$ with the reordered summands [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define $u:X\to C$ by $u(x)=(a(x),-H(x))$ and $q:C\to Y$ by $q(y,z)=y$. All these maps preserve the filtration [def-sp-filtration]. The first component of $d_Cu=ud_X$ is the chain-map identity for $a$, and the second is $d_ZH-sa=-Hd_X$, the displayed homotopy identity. Thus $u$ is a filtered chain map and $qu=a$ strictly. As in step 4, $s\in W$ and [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] imply that every $\operatorname{gr}^i C$ is acyclic, using the grading and shift identifications of step 2 [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients].

source.place: Tag 05RG (lemma-construct-multiplicative-system), dual of its MS3 factorization through the cone; Tags 014E (definition-cone) and 05RT (lemma-acyclic)

proof.text: Now take $T^n=X^n\oplus C^{n-1}$ with $D(x,c)=(d_Xx,-d_Cc-u(x))$, the shifted cone $\operatorname{Cone}(u)[-1]$ with reordered summands, and $t(x,c)=x$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The identity $d_Cu=ud_X$ gives $D^2=0$, and $t$ is a filtered chain map with kernel $C[-1]$. For each $i$, $\operatorname{gr}^i t$ is degreewise surjective with kernel $(\operatorname{gr}^i C)[-1]$, acyclic by step 5, so step 3 gives $t\in W$. The degree $-1$ map $k:T\to C$, $k(x,c)=-c$, is filtered and satisfies $d_Ck+kD=-d_Cc+d_Cc+u(x)=ut$. Since $q$ is a chain map, $qk$ is a filtered homotopy with $d_Y(qk)+(qk)D=qut=at=(f-g)t$. Thus $ft=gt$ in $\mathcal H_f(R)$, proving right cancellation. In expanded coordinates $c=(y,z)$ the differential is $(x,y,z)\mapsto(d_Xx,-d_Yy-a(x),d_Zz+s(y)+H(x))$ and the homotopy $qk$ is $-y$; these formulas also check every sign directly.

source.place: Tag 05RG (lemma-construct-multiplicative-system), right MS3; Tag 014E (definition-cone), explicit shifted-cone null-homotopy

proof.text: The Ore object of step 4 has the common bounds $\min(a_X,a_Y,a_Z)$ and $\max(b_X,b_Y,b_Z)$. The cancellation object has the same bounds, because its summands are $X$, $Y[-1]$ and $Z[-2]$ and a cochain shift does not change the filtration index [def-sp-filtration]. Thus both objects belong to the globally finite subcategory, including when some graded pieces or entire input complexes vanish. Neither construction takes an infinite sum or truncates a complex. The identities and composition property from step 1, the square from step 4 and cancellation from step 6 are precisely the explicit right fraction axioms stated in the item, with the two-out-of-three property already proved. No cochain-degree bound has been imposed.
